threads.body: `get_running_loop()` only describes the thread that is executing this callback. LangChain invokes synchronous `BaseCallbackHandler` methods from async runs in executor workers (and sync tools/models under an async graph can do the same), where this check raises and returns `True`. Those callbacks therefore still attach tokens even though they belong to an async run, so a later callback in another worker can reproduce the cross-context detach failure this change is intended to remove. Make the async/sync mode explicit (or configure this handler to run inline for async callback managers) rather than inferring it from the callback thread.

threads.body: `attach_to_context` remains `True` by default, so an invocation can still be finished in a different runtime context. In that case `detach(context_token)` raises `ValueError`; because it runs before `self.span.end()` in this `finally` block, the exception escapes and the span is never ended. Preserve the previous defensive detach handling (or otherwise guarantee `span.end()` and the original exception are preserved).

threads.body: Setting `run_inline = True` means these callbacks now run directly on the application’s event loop. Since they can do heavier work, including calling a synchronous completion hook, an async LangChain call could block other tasks. Is there a way to fix the context issue without running the entire handler inline?

threads.body:
A running event loop does not necessarily mean LangChain is using its async API. A synchronous `.invoke()` can also be called from an async application. In that case, this check stops the GenAI span from becoming current, so HTTP or database spans created inside the chain may attach to the outer request span instead.

Could we determine whether LangChain is actually using its async callback path?
